meaning_en: To ruin something by overcomplicating it; to add unnecessary embellishment
example_simplified: 他的报告已经很好了，再加内容只是画蛇添足。
example_traditional: 他的報告已經很好了，再加內容只是畫蛇添足。
example_en: His report was already great — adding more was just overcomplicating it.
notes: Yale sourced from CONTEXT.md example.

meaning_en: Wait by a tree stump hoping a rabbit will run into it — rely passively on luck rather than active effort
example_simplified: 光守株待兔是不行的，你应该主动出击。
example_traditional: 光守株待兔是不行的，你應該主動出擊。
example_en: Waiting around for luck to strike won't cut it — you need to take initiative.
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: Play music to a cow — waste effort trying to enlighten someone incapable of appreciating it
example_simplified: 跟他讲道理就是对牛弹琴，他根本不听。
example_traditional: 跟他講道理就是對牛彈琴，他根本不聽。
example_en: Trying to reason with him is like talking to a wall — he simply won't listen.
notes: HK colloquial 雞同鴨講 (gāi tùhng aap gōng) means talking past each other — partial overlap only, not exact equivalent. Yale unverified.

meaning_en: Mend the sheep pen after the sheep is lost — take corrective action after a loss; better late than never
example_simplified: 虽然合同已经签了，但现在修改条款也是亡羊补牢。
example_traditional: 雖然合同已經簽了，但現在修改條款也是亡羊補牢。
example_en: The contract is signed already, but revising the terms now is still better than doing nothing.
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: Give up halfway through; fail to see something through to completion
example_simplified: 学语言不能半途而废，要坚持到底。
example_traditional: 學語言不能半途而廢，要堅持到底。
example_en: You can't quit halfway when learning a language — you have to stick it out.
notes: Used in HK Cantonese speech more than most classical chéngyǔ. Yale unverified.

meaning_en: One cry that astonishes everyone — make a stunning debut after a long period of silence or obscurity
example_simplified: 他沉默多年，这次演出真是一鸣惊人。
example_traditional: 他沉默多年，這次演出真是一鳴驚人。
example_en: He had been quiet for years — this performance was truly a stunning debut.
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: Surrounded on all sides by the songs of Chu — completely isolated and besieged with no allies
example_simplified: 公司陷入四面楚歌的困境，内忧外患同时爆发。
example_traditional: 公司陷入四面楚歌的困境，內憂外患同時爆發。
example_en: The company found itself completely besieged — internal and external crises erupted at once.
notes: References the Battle of Gaixia (202 BC). 楚 (Chó) capitalized as a proper noun. Yale unverified.

meaning_en: Smash the cooking pots and sink the boats — commit fully with no possibility of retreat; burn one's bridges
example_simplified: 他破釜沉舟，辞掉工作全心创业。
example_traditional: 他破釜沉舟，辭掉工作全心創業。
example_en: He went all in — quit his job and committed fully to starting his own business.
notes: Historical origin: Xiang Yu at the Battle of Julu (207 BC). Yale unverified.

meaning_en: A fox borrowing the tiger's authority — bully or intimidate others by exploiting a powerful backer's status
example_simplified: 他不过是狐假虎威，背后的老板才是真正的决策者。
example_traditional: 他不過是狐假虎威，背後的老闆才是真正的決策者。
example_en: He's just riding his boss's coattails — the real decision-maker is behind the scenes.
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: A frog at the bottom of a well — someone with a narrow, limited worldview who is unaware of the wider world
example_simplified: 你不出去看看，就永远是井底之蛙。
example_traditional: 你不出去看看，就永遠是井底之蛙。
example_en: If you never go out and see the world, you'll always be a frog in a well.
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: Mistake a bow's reflection in a cup for a snake — be needlessly fearful or paranoid over something imagined
example_simplified: 别杯弓蛇影，那只是风声，没有人跟踪你。
example_traditional: 別杯弓蛇影，那只是風聲，沒有人跟蹤你。
example_en: Stop being paranoid — that was just the wind; no one is following you.
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: Show off your axe at Lu Ban's door — display mediocre skill in front of an expert; often used self-deprecatingly
example_simplified: 在大师面前谈艺术，真是班门弄斧。
example_traditional: 在大師面前談藝術，真是班門弄斧。
example_en: Talking about art in front of a master — truly showing off in front of an expert.
notes: Lu Ban (魯班) was a legendary craftsman and carpenter. Commonly used as polite self-deprecation. Yale unverified.

meaning_en: Cover your ears while stealing a bell — deceive yourself while fooling no one else; willful self-delusion
example_simplified: 明明有问题还不承认，这不是掩耳盗铃吗？
example_traditional: 明明有問題還不承認，這不是掩耳盜鈴嗎？
example_en: There's clearly a problem and you still won't admit it — isn't that just fooling yourself?
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: Play the yu flute without skill just to make up the numbers — be unqualified but pass oneself off as competent
example_simplified: 团队里有几个人是滥竽充数，根本没有真本事。
example_traditional: 團隊裡有幾個人是濫竽充數，根本沒有真本事。
example_en: A few people on the team are just there to fill seats — they have no real ability.
notes: 竽 is an ancient Chinese reed instrument. Yale unverified.

meaning_en: One's spear contradicts one's shield — to contradict oneself
example_simplified: 你说的话自相矛盾，前后根本不一致。
example_traditional: 你說的話自相矛盾，前後根本不一致。
example_en: What you're saying contradicts itself — your statements are completely inconsistent.
notes: Used in HK speech more than most classical chéngyǔ due to practical everyday application. Yale unverified.

meaning_en: Lord Ye loved dragons — profess great love for something but fear or reject the real thing when faced with it
example_simplified: 他说喜欢挑战，真遇到困难就退缩，真是叶公好龙。
example_traditional: 他說喜歡挑戰，真遇到困難就退縮，真是葉公好龍。
example_en: He claims to love challenges, but when faced with a real one he backs down — all talk.
notes: Yale unverified — flag for native speaker review.

meaning_en: One stone, two birds — accomplish two goals with a single action
example_simplified: 这个方案既省钱又省时，真是一石二鸟。
example_traditional: 這個方案既省錢又省時，真是一石二鳥。
example_en: This plan saves both money and time — truly killing two birds with one stone.
notes: Likely a loan translation of the English idiom; widely used in HK Cantonese speech. Yale unverified.

meaning_en: The horse arrives and success follows — used as a wish for immediate success upon starting something new
example_simplified: 祝你马到成功！
example_traditional: 祝你馬到成功！
example_en: Wishing you immediate success!
notes: Widely used in HK as a blessing, especially around Chinese New Year and new ventures.

meaning_en: One sail, favorable wind — smooth sailing; everything goes well without obstacles
example_simplified: 希望你新的旅程一帆风顺。
example_traditional: 希望你新的旅程一帆風順。
example_en: I hope your new journey goes smoothly all the way.
notes: Common blessing in HK Cantonese, used in cards, toasts, and farewell greetings.

meaning_en: The man from Zheng buys shoes by his measurements rather than trying them on — follow rules rigidly while ignoring practical reality
example_simplified: 你非得照规定来，完全是郑人买履。
example_traditional: 你非得照規定來，完全是鄭人買履。
example_en: Insisting on going strictly by the rulebook when it's clearly impractical — that's the man from Zheng all over.
notes: Relatively obscure; less commonly known in HK Cantonese contexts. Low confidence overall — flag for review. Yale unverified.
